title: Company Operations Lead
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

ElevenLabs moves fast - by design. We run lean, we bias toward action, and we trust our people to figure things out. That's how we've built world-leading AI products in three years with a fraction of the headcount of our peers. But speed at 200 people and speed at 1,000+ people are different challenges, and the systems, habits, and connective tissue that let a company move fast without breaking things don't build themselves.

As our Company Operations Lead, you'll own the infrastructure that lets ElevenLabs keep its velocity as it scales. Not by adding process for process's sake - but by building the right systems, in the right places, at the right time, so that the rest of the company can focus on what they do best. You'll establish the operating layer that keeps a 50-country, hybrid organization coherent; drive the strategic planning cadence that keeps leadership aligned; and deploy a lean team of strategic generalists against the company's most urgent cross-functional challenges.

You’ll be responsible for:

  • Operating Cadence: Running the planning and alignment cycles that keep the company pointed in the right direction. This includes OKR planning, workforce, and headcount planning.

  • Operating System: Building and maintaining the infrastructure layer that lets the company move faster. Systems of record, org taxonomy and governance, and the knowledge management systems that ensure information flow effectively across our remote-first team.

  • AI Enablement & Agentification: Ensuring every team at ElevenLabs has the tools, access, and knowledge to work effectively with AI. You'll own the internal AI enablement framework - managing tool access and rollout, identifying where agents and automation can accelerate how functions operate, and building the learning opportunities and champions programmes that drive deep adoption. You'll work closely with Security, IT, and the Automations team to ensure what gets built is built right.

  • Operations Centre of Excellence: Defining what great operations looks like at ElevenLabs and embedding it across the company. You'll set the blueprint that makes operational excellence repeatable and deploy the team as embedded operators inside other functions, standing up best practices, up-skilling teams, and handing off cleanly once the work is done.

Requirements

We do not require formal experience, certifications, or degrees. We do require:

  • Proven experience building and leading a Strategy & Operations or BizOps function at a high-growth technology company - ideally through a meaningful scaling inflection (Series B–D trajectory or equivalent).

  • Track record of standing up functions and systems from scratch and handing them off, rather than owning a permanent queue.

  • Structured problem-solving background - strategy consulting, a BizOps or Chief of Staff seat with genuine strategic scope, or an operator role that required both systems-building and executive influence.

  • Strong AI and tooling fluency - you should be pushing the organisation on what's possible with AI enablement, not chasing it.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management: you can partner with founders and Leads and earn trust quickly in a flat, high-velocity environment.

Bonus:

  • Experience inside a company that scaled through a 200 → 2,000+ person inflection.

  • Background that spans both consulting and operator roles - you've done the thinking and the building.

  • Familiarity with knowledge management, AI agentification, or internal tooling as an operational discipline.

Location

This role is remote. London or New York preferred.

#LI-Remote

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

title: Senior Manager, Supplier Performance, FinCrime, Fraud & Disputes
description:
🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save, invest and combine their pensions with us.

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

📍London/Cardiff/UK Remote | 💰£68,400-86,550 + equity + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits ✨

Our FinCrime, Fraud & Disputes teams⭐

We are recruiting a Senior Manager to join our FinCrime, Fraud and Disputes team, whilst supporting our Supplier Performance function. Outsourcing is key to enabling Monzo to meet its mission of making money work for everyone, as well as driving a cost efficient operation and delivering excellent customer service.

We are changing how we manage our relationships with our outsourcing partners by driving more responsibility and accountability through our Monzo domain leaders. We need a brilliant Seniors Managers to join this new oversight team, reporting directly to the Directors within each business area.

Partner management is moving right into the heart of our domains. You will be our eyes and ears on the ground, making sure our offshore outsource partners feel like a true extension of Monzo and not just an outsourced supplier. We ensure our partners are set up for success and deliver fantastic customer service.


🔑You’ll play a key role by...

You will act as the vital bridge between Monzo and our external partners to ensure they feel like a true extension of our team. You will drive both operational delivery and a brilliant customer experience. Working closely with our site leaders in South Africa, you will manage day to day service delivery while keeping a close eye on quality, customer satisfaction, and risk management. A key part of your role involves translating our strategic business goals into clear, actionable steps for the partner management team so they are fully equipped to succeed. You will support in domain forecasting and rolling out new processes to make sure they actually work on the floor. Ultimately, you will integrate our partner leaders into our regular performance reviews to foster a genuine one team mindset across the operation.

  • Leading a dedicated oversight team: You will directly manage a Supplier Operations Partner who wil focus on Operational Delivery like SLAs, schedule adherence, Customer Experience, quality, and fixing the root causes of repeat contacts.
  • Managing the partnership day to day: You will work directly with our outsourced partner Operations Managers to ensure the whole domain is delivering the service, customer satisfaction, quality and risk management we expect.
  • Acting as the translation layer: You will turn our strategic business goals into practical, actionable steps for the outsouring management team. You will make sure they are equipped to succeed, rather than just telling them when they miss the mark.
  • Tracking and managing performance: You will work alongside our partners to oversee all aspects of day to day service management, including handling risk events and stepping in to engage partners directly when performance drifts.
  • Forecasting and planning: Alongside WFM you will raise and approve forecast requests and manage the end to end domain forecasting process for our partners.
  • Owning change execution: You will handle the end to end definition and execution of change through our partners, ensuring any new processes or solutions are actually fit for purpose on the floor.
  • Integrating the teams: You will support the domain Director to embed Teleperformance leaders into our existing domain performance review meetings, fostering a one team mindset.

🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…

  • You have proven track record of working closely with or managing global offshore partners and can manage to a customer experience, not just a commercial contract.
  • You are deeply analytical mindset with the ability to anchor decisions in rigorous data, translating complex metrics into robust business cases that secure senior stakeholder buy in.
  • You have a proven track record of leading through others and can influence, coach, and guide Managers who do not report directly to you.
  • You are brilliant at translating complex business goals into simple steps for frontline teams.
  • You zoom out when solving operational problems. Don’t just look at the operational team, always think about how your decisions impact the rest of the business.

Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! Studies show that women and people of colour might hesitate to apply unless they meet every single requirement. At Monzo, we’re dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming team. If you’re passionate about this role and keen to learn and grow with us, we encourage you to apply— even if you don’t have everything that's listed just yet. Drop us your application, we’d love to hear from you!

🙌 What’s in it for you

💰 £68,400-86,550 + equity + Incentive Awards tied to your performance

⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team.

📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.

🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup.

➕ Plus lots more! Read our full list of benefits.

🌈 The application journey has 3 key steps

  • Recruiter call (25 minutes)
  • Values & Behaviours Interview (60 minutes)
  • Role Specific Interview (60 minutes)

This process should take around 3-4 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible!

We have some guidelines on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to ace an application and interview at Monzo. You can read them here.

We’ll only close this role once we have enough applications for the next stage. Please submit your application as soon as possible to make sure you don’t miss out.

#LI-REMOTE #LI-CB4

Equal opportunities for everyone

Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our blog, 2026 Diversity and Inclusion Report and 2025 Gender Pay Gap Report.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.

Backed by Sequoia Capital, Coatue Management, NVIDIA, Snowflake and other leading investors, we have been in business for over a decade but are still a small team operating with the spirit of a startup. In the world of AI today, we believe that the future is still being invented — and we want to be the ones building it. For more information, visit www.domino.ai

What we are building

Domino's Solutions team is the customer-facing engine behind how leading enterprises build, scale, and govern AI-powered applications - solving real business challenges, not just deploying technology. Solutions Engineering earns technical credibility before the deal closes. Customer Engineering, where this role lives, owns everything after: adoption, implementation, expansion, and the kind of delivery that makes customers renew and grow. Global Support and SRE keeps it all running at the level enterprise customers depend on. Three functions, one relentless motion, and a team that earns its reputation on what it ships, not what it scopes.

What your impact will be

  • Own the customer program end-to-end: from contract signature through expansion. You're accountable for outcomes, not activities, and every engagement you lead has a single owner (you), clear milestones, and a cadence that keeps everyone (internally and externally) moving as the program manager.
  • Partner with account team to ensure every engagement is scoped to be delivered with excellence, bridging what is sold with what can be executed.
  • Direct the delivery pod (our Forward Deployed Engineers and Integration & Architecture teams) for customer engagements. Put capacity where it creates the most value and keep programs on track across milestones, stakeholder communication, and account health.
  • Earn trust at every level: from C-suite sponsors to the data scientists running models in production. You close the gap between strategic intent and day-to-day delivery.
  • Lead the room in solutioning conversations: connect how Domino builds, scales, and governs AI to the outcomes customer leadership actually cares about. You operate as a peer, not a vendor.
  • Make adoption real: drive rollout, enablement, and change management so what your team ships gets used, not shelved.
  • Turn customer engagements into growth in partnership with customer success and sales — proactively uncovering new use cases and expansion opportunities, qualifying them, and routing them back to internal teams to fuel pipeline.
  • Be the customer's voice inside Domino: convert field intelligence into product feedback, escalations, and commercial signals that make the broader team smarter.

What we look for in this role

  • 4–8 years in an enterprise customer-facing discipline: implementations, consulting, technical program management, or product. Caliber and complexity matter more than the title.
  • Background in life sciences where reproducibility, auditability, and compliance are non-negotiable is a meaningful advantage.
  • Comfortable owning the what, not just the when: you can reshape a customer's ask into the right solution, even when that means pushing back on the original scope
  • You move before the problem is fully formed: comfortable when the customer can't yet articulate what's wrong and treating ambiguity as the starting point.
  • You turn unstructured executive conversations into executable plans: connecting model development, deployment, and governance without losing what actually matters.
  • You know enough about how enterprise data science teams build, scale, and govern models to ask the right questions before the customer knows they need to answer them.
  • Real delivery ownership across full cycles, not coordination. You hold an execution rhythm, hold a position when things get hard, and don't create bureaucracy to do it.
  • Technically fluent across software architecture, predictive modeling, and agentic systems: able to get hands-on when it matters and learn new domains fast.
  • Solutions-oriented by default. You escalate with a recommendation, not just a problem, and reach for AI to do all of it faster and better.

What we value

  • We strongly believe in the value of growing a diverse team and encourage people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, abilities, and sexual orientations to apply
  • We value a growth mindset. High-performing creative individuals who dig into problems and see the opportunities for success
  • We believe in individuals who seek truth and speak the truth and can be their whole selves at work
  • We value all of you that believe improving is always possible. At Domino, everything is a work in progress – we can do better at everything
  • We emphasize an environment of teaching and learning to equip employees with the tools needed to be successful in their function and the company

description:
Who we are

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

As a Senior Engineer in the Infrastructure org, you will help evolve the cloud foundations behind every Samsara product. Your goal will be to reduce systemic production risk and enable continued growth by making infrastructure safer to change, easier to operate, and more resilient and cost-efficient at scale.

You will bring deep expertise in at least one infrastructure domain, such as compute and workload orchestration, networking, storage and stateful systems, or cloud control planes, and apply it across our multi-account, multi-region AWS environment. You will lead work such as modernizing compute and stateful infrastructure, strengthening capacity and failure isolation, and building standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation.

You will partner with product engineering teams to turn recurring risks and manual operations into durable platforms and paved paths. We do not expect you to be an expert in every infrastructure domain. We are looking for engineers who have built and operated critical systems at significant scale, understand how infrastructure fails, and can use that experience to improve both our platforms and our engineering practices.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact, helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go.
  • You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes.
  • You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we’re all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win together.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and operate reliable cloud platforms, bringing depth in one or more areas such as compute, networking, storage, stateful systems, or infrastructure control planes.
  • Improve the scalability, capacity management, isolation, recovery, and cost efficiency of critical production infrastructure.
  • Build standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation that support self-service provisioning, testing, progressive rollout, reconciliation, rollback, and drift prevention.
  • Identify shared failure modes and build safeguards that prevent localized failures from escalating into broad customer impact.
  • Contribute to multi-account, multi-region, and isolated AWS architectures, including regulated environments such as GovCloud.
  • Participate in operational ownership and incident response, using incidents and near misses to drive durable architectural improvements.
  • Mentor engineers, raise the quality of infrastructure design and operational judgment, and establish patterns that can be adopted across the organization.
  • Clearly communicate architecture, trade-offs, risks, and migration plans to technical and organizational stakeholders.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for this role.

  • 6+ years of experience designing and building software, infrastructure, or distributed systems, including operating critical systems in production.
  • Deep expertise in at least one of the following: compute and workload orchestration, networking, storage and stateful systems, or cloud infrastructure control planes.
  • Strong software-engineering fundamentals in Go, Python, Java, or a similar language.
  • Hands-on experience designing and operating infrastructure on a major public cloud platform; AWS experience is preferred.
  • Experience using infrastructure as code, such as Terraform, to safely manage production infrastructure.
  • Strong understanding of capacity management, failure domains, observability, rollout safety, and production recovery.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives across teams and through ambiguous problem spaces.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Designing and operating large-scale compute or container platforms such as ECS, EKS, Kubernetes, or similar orchestration systems.
  • Designing and operating stateful distributed systems such as Kafka, OpenSearch, managed databases, caching, or large-scale storage platforms.
  • Building internal infrastructure platforms, control planes, or self-service developer experiences adopted across multiple teams.
  • Designing multi-account or multi-region cloud architectures with strong workload isolation and disaster recovery.
  • Leading major infrastructure migrations while maintaining availability and controlling operational risk.
  • Delivering measurable improvements in infrastructure capacity, cost efficiency, or developer self-service.

Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. title: Learning Support Assistant
description:
We are seeking to appoint a caring, reliable and enthusiastic Learning Support Assistant to join our small and supportive Learning Support Department. Working under the guidance of the SENCo and alongside the existing Learning Support Assistant and teaching staff, you will play an important role in supporting students with additional learning needs, helping them overcome barriers to learning and make the most of their education.

You will be joining The Latymer School at an exciting time as we work towards completing the build of our new modern and impressive Library and Learning Resource Centre. Moreover, as we enter our 402nd year, we are extremely proud of our history and tradition, whilst also seeking to continue to modernise and ensure every aspect of our school prepares our young people well for life in modern Britain.

The Learning Support Department works with students across the school, providing support tailored to their individual needs. Our approach focuses on helping students develop their confidence, organisation and independence, supporting their social and emotional wellbeing and ensuring they can access and participate in mainstream lessons. Support may take place in the classroom, through individual or small-group interventions, or at other times during the school day.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who is passionate about supporting young people and wants to make a positive difference to their school experience. You will work closely with the SENCo, the other Learning Support Assistant and teaching staff, building supportive relationships with students and helping them develop the skills and confidence to become more independent learners.

A further detailed job description and person specification is attached in the candidate pack.

Further details about The Latymer School can be found on the school website (www.latymer.co.uk): The Latymer School - Join our team. If, after reading the information, you are interested in joining us please cre﻿ate an account at MyNewTermand submit your application.

The school provides a range of well-being activities and facilities including good transport links, free parking, a cycle to work scheme, use of the fitness suite, Pilates at an affordable cost and massages by a qualified masseuse. We also run a number of national and international trips and have our own residential centre in a beautiful part of North Wales, which staff can also use. We value our staff and recognise the importance of maintaining a healthy work-life balance

If you would like to join our friendly and supportive school community and make a positive contribution to the lives of our students, we would be delighted to hear from you

The Latymer School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of young people. We expect all staff to share this commitment. Any offer of employment is subject to a satisfactory ‘Enhanced with a Barred List Check’ through the Disclosure and Barring Service.

As part of our selection and appointment process, and in accordance with Keeping Children Safe in Education guidance, we are required to conduct online searches on all candidates in order to identify any incidents or concerns which are publicly available online. By submitting and signing your application, you acknowledge that such searches will be conducted as part of the selection and appointment process.

The Latymer School is an equal opportunities employer.

title: Finance Business Partner
description:
Finance Business Partner

Job Role: Finance Business Partner

Location: Newham Community Learning Trust Central Office, Pretoria Rd, London E16 4NP (Eastlea Community School)

Closing Date: 22nd November 2026

Newham Community Learning is a Multi-Academy Trust serving children and young people in East London. We believe every young person deserves an excellent education, whatever their background. Our commitment to equality and social justice shapes how we lead, how we spend, and how we hold ourselves to account.


About this Role

We are looking for an experienced and detail-focused finance Business Partner to join our Trust Finance Team. Working closely with the Chief Finance Officer and Financial Controller, you will play a key role in delivering accurate and effective financial accounting processes across the Trust, supporting strong financial controls, compliance and high-quality financial reporting.

You will take responsibility for a range of monthly and year-end accounting processes, including balance sheet and control account reconciliations, accruals and prepayments, intercompany transactions, trial balances, cashflow forecasting and fixed asset records. You will also prepare payroll journals and reconciliations, support VAT and statutory returns, and contribute to the annual external audit process, including ESFA and DfE reporting, HMRC and pension-related submissions.

Working closely with our schools, you will help ensure financial transactions are accurate, timely and compliant with Trust policies and procedures. You will also liaise with our payroll provider and work alongside the CFO, Financial Controller and Procurement Manager to ensure financial processes are robust, consistent and delivered within required deadlines.

The role will also provide an opportunity to contribute to the continued development and improvement of our financial accounting systems and processes, including PS Financials.

What We’re Looking For

We are looking for someone who:

  • Has strong financial accounting experience and a sound understanding of accounting principles and financial controls.

  • Has experience of preparing and reviewing reconciliations, journals, accruals, prepayments and balance sheet accounts.

  • Is confident working with monthly and year-end financial processes and meeting strict deadlines.

  • Has excellent attention to detail and takes pride in ensuring financial information is accurate, complete and reliable.

  • Has experience supporting external audits, statutory accounts and financial returns.

  • Understands the importance of compliance, governance and financial procedures.

  • Has strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate discrepancies and resolve issues effectively.

  • Is confident working with financial systems and spreadsheets; experience of PS Financials would be advantageous.

  • Can communicate effectively with colleagues across schools, senior leaders, auditors and external organisations.

  • Is organised, proactive and able to manage competing priorities in a busy finance environment.

  • Works collaboratively and is committed to providing a high-quality financial service across the Trust

This is an excellent opportunity for a finance professional with strong financial accounting experience who is looking to make a meaningful contribution to a growing Trust and play an important role in maintaining high standards of financial management and accountability.

Why Join Us?

  • Be part of a forward-thinking multi-academy Trust, making a real impact on staff and students.

  • Local Government Pension Scheme.

  • Generous annual leave entitlement

  • A supportive, values-led culture in the heart of London.

  • Access to professional development and training opportunities.

  • Employee wellbeing initiatives and a focus on work-life balance.

title: Lead Teacher of Reading Intervention - Secondary
description:
We are a highly supportive school, backed by strong subject leadership and senior management, dedicated to fostering professional development and excellence in teaching and learning. We are seeking a highly ambitious, committed and dynamic professional to take on the newly created role of Lead Teacher of Reading Intervention. This is an exciting opportunity for an individual who is passionate about literacy and committed to improving outcomes for students who require intensive reading support.

The successful candidate will lead and deliver our reading intervention strategy for students Years 7 to 11 whose reading skills are significantly below age-related expectations. Working directly with some of our most vulnerable learners, you will help students develop the reading, phonics, and literacy skills they need to access the secondary curriculum successfully.

The postholder will be line managed by a member of the Senior Leadership Team and will work closely with the Secondary Literacy Lead, SEND and Inclusion Teams, curriculum leaders and families to ensure targeted support is effective and impactful. The role will also involve working cross-phase with primary colleagues where appropriate, supporting continuity in reading provision and successful transition into secondary education.

The role would particularly suit an experienced primary practitioner with a strong understanding of phonics, reading development and literacy intervention who is ready for the challenge of working in a secondary setting. Equally, we welcome applications from secondary colleagues with expertise in reading intervention. The successful candidate will be passionate about securing rapid progress for students whose low reading ages act as a barrier to learning.

The successful candidate will lead the assessment of reading and spelling ages across the Academy, co-ordinate diagnostic assessments, analyse literacy data and evaluate the impact of interventions. They will use this information to develop a coherent programme of support that is evidence-informed, targeted and responsible to student need.

Intervention delivery forms a central part of the role. The successful candidate will plan and deliver high-quality one-to-one, small-group, timetabled literacy interventions, adapting provision to meet individual needs and ensuring accelerated progress in reading. They will create an inclusive environment where students develop confidence and success as readers. The role may also include teaching some KS3 English, where appropriate, to further support students’ literacy development and access to the wider curriculum.

Collaboration is at the heart of this role. The successful candidate will work closely with curriculum leaders to identify barriers within different subject areas and support staff in developing strategies that improve literacy across the curriculum. They will also engage positively with parents and carers and contribute to the Academy’s wider literacy strategy.

The successful candidate will have a passion for teaching and learning, excellent communication and organisational skills, and a strong understanding of literacy development and intervention planning. Experience of phonics teaching and supporting young people with significant reading gaps will be essential. Above all, they will share our determination that every student, regardless of starting point, can access, engage with and succeed within the secondary curriculum through improved literacy and reading.

Visiting the school prior to submission of an application is warmly encouraged.

Our commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our children will be reflected throughout the recruitment process and the successful applicant will be subject to an enhanced DBS check and an online screening check.

Prospective candidates are encouraged to submit their applications as soon as possible as the school reserves the right to close the advert should we feel able to appoint an appropriate candidate.

description:
Are you passionate about the leisure industry and ready to take the next step in your career? Do you enjoy leading teams, delivering excellent customer service and ensuring leisure facilities operate safely and effectively?

We are looking for a motivated and enthusiastic Leisure Centre Duty Manager to join Lift Sir Herbert Leon Leisure Centre. This is an exciting opportunity for someone with previous leisure industry experience who is ready to take on a leadership role and contribute to the successful day-to-day management of a busy leisure facility.

About the role

As our Leisure Centre Duty Manager, you will play a key role in supporting the day-to-day operations of the Leisure Centre, ensuring a safe, welcoming and high-quality experience for all customers and visitors.

You will be responsible for supporting and supervising staff, maintaining high standards of customer service, ensuring compliance with health and safety regulations and contributing to the effective management of the Centre's facilities and activities.

Your responsibilities will include overseeing swimming pool operations, carrying out pool water tests and plant maintenance, lifeguarding swimming sessions and ensuring all facilities and equipment are maintained to a high standard.

You will also support staff recruitment, training and development, assist with the planning and delivery of leisure programmes and activities, and help promote the Centre's services to the wider community.

As part of the management team, you will act as a keyholder, support emergency procedures and ensure the Centre operates safely and efficiently in accordance with established policies and procedures.

About you

You will already hold an NPLQ Lifeguard Qualification and have previous experience working within a leisure centre environment. You will have strong team leadership skills and the confidence to support colleagues while maintaining excellent standards of service.

You will be:

  • Friendly, confident and customer-focused
  • An effective team leader who leads by example
  • Able to communicate effectively with colleagues and customers
  • Knowledgeable about leisure centre operations and committed to maintaining high standards of health and safety
  • Organised, reliable and able to respond effectively to operational challenges
  • Flexible and willing to support different areas of the Leisure Centre
  • Committed to providing a safe and welcoming environment for everyone using our facilities
  • Keen to contribute to the ongoing development and improvement of the Centre

GCSE Maths and English at Grade 4 or above, or an equivalent Level 2 qualification, are essential for the role.

Additional qualifications and experience, including a Level 1 or 2 Swimming Teacher Qualification, Pool Plant Operator Certificate, First Aid at Work Certificate or previous management experience, would be advantageous.

About Lift Sir Herbert Leon Leisure Centre

At the heart of our community, Lift Sir Herbert Leon Leisure Centre offers excellent fitness and sports facilities, including a swimming pool, gym, multi-purpose sports hall, 3G Astro-turf and grass pitches - everything needed to support active, healthy lifestyles for students and the local community.

As part of Lift Schools, you will be joining an organisation committed to ensuring every child receives an excellent education, in every classroom, every day.

Who is Lift Schools?

Lift Schools is made up of 62 primary, secondary and special schools, educating more than 35,000 pupils across the country. We believe education can transform lives - and we want every child in our schools to achieve their full potential.






This is a full-time position (37 hours per week), with a start date as soon as possible.

The Windsor Boys’ School is seeking to appoint an enthusiastic, organised and reliable Science Technician to join our successful and supportive Science Department. This is an exciting opportunity to become part of a thriving department, supporting the delivery of high-quality Science education across Biology, Chemistry and Physics. Working alongside our teaching staff, you will play an important role in preparing practical resources, maintaining equipment and ensuring that our laboratories provide a safe, well-equipped and stimulating learning environment.

We are able to offer flexibility, with both full-time and part-time working arrangements available for the right candidate.

At The Windsor Boys’ School, you will join a committed team with a strong culture of collaboration and a shared ambition to provide excellent opportunities for our pupils.

For further information about the role, please refer to the accompanying job description. We warmly welcome applications from candidates who would like to contribute to the continued success of our Science Department.

Windsor Learning Partnership is committed to safeguarding children and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. If you are interested in applying for this position, please access the school’s website where further information can be found: www.twbs.co.uk

JOB DESCRIPTION

Job Purpose

To assist subject teachers in the delivery of the curriculum by preparing the teaching area and equipment for pupils.

Scope of Job (budgetary/resource control, impact)

Operates within a specialised subject environment such as a laboratory or workshop.

Works with a variety of materials, which require appropriate handling and application.

Involved in moving equipment/materials.

Will have contact directly with pupils and will be required to deal with them in a sympathetic manner

Will spend majority of working time standing and undertaking physical activities.

Due to the nature of the activities special attention must be paid to Health & Safety issues both for the environment and equipment/materials used.

Position within Unit Structure

Reports to Head of Department.

Knowledge, Skills and Experience

Physically fit, able to lift heavy/awkward items.

Able to, or willingness to learn to operate, maintain and repair a variety of specialist equipment

Must have manual dexterity.

Knowledge of specialist products relevant to the subject area

Able to remain calm in a busy environment.

Develop and maintain knowledge of current developments in their specialist area.

Qualified to A level or NVQ 2 or equivalent by experience in a specialist area eg biology, physics

First Aid - appointed person or fully qualified?

Job Accountabilities

In line with the instructions from the subject teacher prepare the specified materials and equipment in time for the specified lesson. This will include preparing complex equipment/experiments to enable the teacher to demonstrate experiments safely or preparing materials for pupils to use during lessons.

Maintain sufficient supplies of materials, chemicals etc to enable teachers to deliver their lessons. This will include placing orders with suppliers and ensuring that items are purchased in a cost-effective way.

Undertake regular checks of the more complex/sensitive equipment, ensuring annual maintenance/safety checks are completed.

Undertake daily cleaning of used equipment and maintenance. Undertake periodic cleaning of equipment in line with Departments timetable.

Ensure that all allocated equipment and materials are stored safely and securely to prevent unauthorised access and potential accidents/misuse.

Under the direction of the subject teacher work with pupils in the classroom/laboratory/workshop supporting and encouraging their learning by explaining/demonstrating exercises/experiments etc.

Perform duties in line with Health & Safety rules and to take remedial action where hazards are identified. Where hazards are serious report to the line manager immediately.

Undertake First Aid duties in line with qualification/training received and act in line with the school’s accident/incident policy

title: Senior Designated Safeguarding Lead
description:
Creating Great Futures

At Croydon College Group, our staff are passionate and committed to achieving the very best outcomes for our students. We recognise that our people are our greatest asset, and through their expertise, dedication, and commitment, we deliver an outstanding student experience that positively impacts our local community. Our values of being Caring, Collaborative, Courageous and Creative underpin everything we do, ensuring we create an inclusive, supportive and ambitious environment for both students and staff.

We are seeking an exceptional safeguarding professional to join our Student Services leadership team as our Senior Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL). This is a pivotal leadership role responsible for providing strategic and operational oversight of safeguarding, wellbeing, Prevent, and student protection across the College Group.

As the College's lead safeguarding professional, you will ensure the highest standards of safeguarding practice, compliance, and culture, while leading a dedicated safeguarding team across both campuses. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced safeguarding leader to shape and strengthen safeguarding provision within a dynamic and student-centred FE environment.

The Role

Reporting directly to the Executive Director of Student Services, you will act as the College's Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL), ensuring compliance with statutory safeguarding requirements and providing expert advice to senior leaders, governors, staff and external agencies. You will lead safeguarding strategy, oversee complex and high-risk cases, drive quality assurance and continuous improvement, and promote a culture where students feel safe, supported and empowered to thrive.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Operational & System Management: Managing safeguarding records and ensuring full, effective use of our CPOMS system.
  • Compliance & Best Practice: Ensuring overall team compliance with regulatory standards, covering both reactive management and proactive safeguarding initiatives.
  • Case & Team Leadership: Overseeing incoming disclosures, managing risk assessments, and supporting team members in day-to-day safeguarding operations.

In addition, you will:

  • Lead safeguarding, Prevent and contextual safeguarding strategy across the College Group.
  • Provide expert oversight and decision-making for complex safeguarding and risk cases.
  • Act as the key safeguarding adviser to senior leaders, governors and external partners.
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with Children's Social Care, Adult Social Care, CAMHS, Police, Prevent partners and other agencies.
  • Lead safeguarding quality assurance, audits, thematic reviews and compliance activity.
  • Manage and develop the safeguarding team, ensuring high standards of practice and performance.
  • Lead safeguarding training, awareness and culture across the organisation.
  • Prepare safeguarding reports, trend analysis and assurance updates for senior leaders and governors.

About You

We are looking for an experienced and highly credible safeguarding leader who brings extensive expertise, sound judgement, and the ability to lead with confidence in a complex educational environment.

Key Requirements:

  • Substantial operational experience leading safeguarding within a FE / HE / college setting.
  • Advanced proficiency with CPOMS and safeguarding record-keeping.
  • Strong knowledge of current statutory guidance and compliance requirements.

You will also demonstrate:

  • Significant safeguarding leadership experience within Further Education, education, or a comparable multi-site environment.
  • Experience managing complex safeguarding and high-risk cases.
  • Experience leading safeguarding teams and driving improvements in practice.
  • Expert knowledge of Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE), safeguarding legislation and regulatory requirements.
  • Strong understanding of Prevent, contextual safeguarding, vulnerable adults, mental health and inclusion.
  • Excellent leadership, communication, partnership-building and decision-making skills.
  • The professional resilience, integrity and commitment required to safeguard and promote the welfare of learners.

title: Higher Level Teaching Assistant
description:
We seek an individual who is keen to give quality support to students' learning and behaviour and support the whole school drive for improved literacy. Taking on a specialist role to deliver targeted interventions in literacy, the successful candidate will support a wide range of students with complex, diverse learning needs and take responsibility for ensuring they make progress in literacy and across the curriculum. The successful applicant will also be involved in breakfast club, break and lunch time support, study club, after school clubs and/or in the Additional Resourced Provision for SEND students, according to need.

About Greenford High School

Our vision is to be ‘ambitious for all’, and over the last decade we have consistently achieved outcomes that have placed us in the top 20% of schools nationally for student progress. We aim for all students to achieve excellent academic results, but we are also a truly comprehensive school which tries to get the best out of every child, whatever their ability or circumstances. We are known for our exceptionally strong relationships between staff and students and for our staff promotion opportunities across many areas of the school.

Our facilities are superb with a university campus style layout, extensive IT facilities, large, expansive playing fields. We also have one of the largest Post-16 Centres in London with designated study and support areas.

As well as working alongside friendly, supportive colleagues, what does GHS offer you?

  • a supportive approach to approving staff leave of absences;

  • small class sizes where possible;

  • financial assistance for Masters and further degrees;

  • a partnership with the Institute of Education and Teach First;

  • free on-site car parking spaces and secure bicycle storage;

  • free access to sporting facilities and fitness gym;

  • a range of health & well-being services including access to the ‘Workplace Options’ staff support scheme and onsite counselling;

Job Description

Purpose of the post: To work with teaching staff to support the whole school drive for improved literacy. The postholder will take on a specialist role to lead on delivering targeted interventions in literacy, reading, writing and communication. The postholder will support a wide range of students with complex and diverse learning needs and take responsibility for ensuring they make progress in literacy, across the curriculum and in line with school priorities.

Accountable to: Assistant Headteacher - SENCO and Assistant Headteacher - Literacy

Responsible for: Delivering literacy interventions, as directed by Assistant Headteacher - Literacy. Supporting a range of students with complex needs, as directly by the Assistant Headteacher - SENCO

Duties:

  • Be responsible for leading on the delivery, monitoring and tracking of progress in literacy for an identified group of students.

  • To work closely with the Assistant Headteacher - Literacy to ensure interventions remain fit for student needs and are achieving positive outcomes.

  • To work closely with parents and carers ensuring the best possible outcome for an identified group of students.

  • To work collaboratively with teachers to share strategies and progress of an identified group of students.

  • To develop strong communication with parents, carers and family and give support to help them use consistent behaviour management at home.

  • To monitor progress, set targets and ensure that the appropriate intervention strategies are put into place for a small cohort of identified students.

  • To help teachers plan to support learning and progress for the identified students.

  • To support the academic, social and emotional progress of identified students with complex needs.

  • To help the students develop resilience and independence, both learning in lessons and in having positive peer & staff relationships.

  • To support the school’s inclusion centre as directed, working with students who may be in danger of permanent exclusion.

  • To undertake work and responsibilities in line with the Training and Development Agency for Schools (TDA) Standards for Higher Level Teaching Assistants.

  • To support development of students’ resilience and independence, in classrooms and around the school.

  • To run small group activities to help the student meet their targets.

  • To be supportive of the student’s social development before and after school and at breaktimes by running enrichment activities in the playground.

  • To promote the inclusion of all pupils, ensuring they have equal opportunities to learn and develop

  • To participate in appropriate meetings with colleagues and parents to facilitate the proper execution of the postholder’s responsibilities.

  • To undertake a share of general supervisory duties in accordance with the school’s organisation of duty rosters.

  • To provide support to students with exam arrangements. Completing training to ensure compliance.

  • To support with SEN coffee mornings.

title: Graduate Maths Excellence Specialist
description:
Love maths? Inspire the next generation and kick-start your teaching career!


Are you a maths graduate with a passion for your subject and a desire to make a real difference to young people's lives?

Co-op Academies Trust has an exciting opportunity for a number of Graduate Maths Excellence Specialists to join us on a two-year fixed term contract, supporting high-achieving pupils to reach their full potential in mathematics.

This is more than just a graduate role. It's an opportunity to gain valuable classroom experience, develop your teaching skills and take the first steps towards a rewarding career in education.


What will you be doing?

Working alongside experienced maths teachers and subject leaders, you'll help inspire and challenge pupils, particularly high-attaining disadvantaged students, to achieve their very best.

You will:

  1. Deliver engaging maths sessions to individuals, small groups and classes.
  2. Support pupils studying GCSE Mathematics, GCSE Statistics and Level 2 Further Mathematics.
  3. Develop creative resources, enrichment activities and masterclasses that bring maths to life.
  4. Mentor pupils, monitor their progress and help build their confidence and aspirations.
  5. Work closely with teaching and pastoral colleagues to support pupils' achievement and wellbeing.
  6. Gain hands-on classroom experience and develop the skills needed for a future career in teaching.


What are we looking for?

We're looking for enthusiastic graduates who love mathematics and can share that enthusiasm with young people.

You'll need a degree in mathematics or a closely related subject with substantial mathematical content (50% minimum), strong communication skills and the confidence to engage and motivate pupils.

Previous experience working with young people would be an advantage, but we're equally interested in your potential, enthusiasm and commitment to making a difference.

You'll also need to be committed to safeguarding, inclusion and creating a positive learning environment for every pupil.


Where could this opportunity take you?

This two-year programme offers a unique pathway into teaching with Co-op Academies Trust.

Following your fixed-term appointment, you will have the opportunity to progress to our teacher training programme, subject to meeting the relevant entry requirements, with the opportunity to continue your career as a qualified mathematics teacher within the Trust.

You'll benefit from practical experience, professional development and support from experienced colleagues as you prepare for your teaching career.


Ready to turn your passion for maths into a career that makes a difference?

Apply today and take your first step towards inspiring the next generation of mathematicians.


Want to hear more before applying?

Webinars will run on Wed 18th Nov at 4pm. Please follow the link to sign up https://www.coopacademies.co.uk/graduate-maths-excellence-specialist


Co-op Academies Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. The successful candidate will be subject to an enhanced DBS check and other relevant pre-employment checks. We are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcome applications from all backgrounds.

title: BA/Technical Product Manager
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: https://jobs.workable.com/company/u8TybTAE2YbYgRVFYov9t4/jobs-at-proarch

 Partner Discovery & Requirements Analysis
 • Lead and document working sessions with clinical, finance, operations, product, and technical stakeholders to understand existing workflows, business rules, data requirements, and operational processes.
• Translate manual and system-supported workflows into structured business and functional requirements.
• Produce gap-analysis documentation mapping current-state processes and partner requirements to existing platform capabilities.
• Classify requirements based on appropriate disposition, such as existing functionality, configuration, new development, acceptable operational workaround, shared platform enhancement, or out of scope.
• Maintain a consistent backlog structure across implementations so requirements remain comparable, traceable, and reusable.
 System Reconciliation & Technical Analysis
 • Analyze application logic, SQL, stored procedures, configuration parameters, integrations, and data flows to understand existing system behavior.
• Determine whether business requirements can be satisfied through configuration, existing functionality, process changes, or new development.
• Validate assumptions about platform behavior against available technical evidence and distinguish confirmed system behavior from inferred behavior.
• Identify discrepancies between documented behavior, stakeholder expectations, system configuration, and implemented logic.
• Trace business rules to underlying parameters, data elements, calculations, integrations, and system components.
• Identify where behaviors are configurable versus hardcoded and assess the impact on future implementations.
 Requirements Authoring
 • Write clear business and functional requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, assumptions, dependencies, open questions, and proposed workarounds.
• Maintain appropriate separation between business-facing requirements and technical implementation details.
• Ensure acceptance criteria reflect the agreed solution approach, including configuration changes, operational workarounds, or new functionality.
• Apply a consistent standard for distinguishing standalone requirements from assumptions, configuration decisions, implementation details, or operational procedures.
• Maintain traceability from business need through solution decision and development implementation.
 Cross-Functional Facilitation & Governance

title: Senior Backend Cloud Engineer
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: http://www.halcyon.ai

 What we do:
Halcyon is the industry’s first dedicated, adaptive security platform that combines multiple proprietary advanced prevention engines along with AI models focused specifically on stopping ransomware.

 Who we are:
Halcyon was formed in 2021 by a team of cyber industry veterans after battling the scourge of ransomware (and advanced threats) for years at some of the largest global security vendors. Comprised of leaders from Cylance (now Blackberry), Accuvant (now Optiv), Fireye and ISS X-Force (now IBM), Halcyon is focused on building products and solutions for mid-market and enterprise customers.

 As a remote-native, completely distributed global team, we recognize great talent can exist anywhere. We invite you to apply to a job you’re interested in and we'll work a plan to meet your needs.

 The Role

 At Halcyon, we’re building a world-class anti-ransomware platform grounded in innovation and resilience. As part of that vision, we’re looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join our cloud team. You’ll lead the development and evolution of our data platform and API services, working within a modern tech stack that blends Scala and Rust.

 You’ll join a team focused on building scalable, maintainable backend systems that serve both internal and customer-facing functions. Your primary focus will be on Rust and Scala services, with opportunities to shape our transition to Rust where it makes sense. Python development experience is highly valued, particularly for supporting our security analysis platform which includes malware analysis engines, automated threat detection, and machine learning workflows.

 Responsibilities

• Lead the design and delivery of features across our data platform and public API services, including ingestion, transformation, and enrichment of security data.

• Drive system design, architecture, and data flow decisions in partnership with product and platform engineering.

• Build, deploy, and own Scala-based backend services in production, keeping them reliable, secure, and performant.

• Help shape and execute our migration of selected APIs from Scala to Rust, ensuring consistency and continuity along the way.

• Set the bar for code quality, documentation, and operational excellence.

• Lead design reviews, code reviews and take part in on-call and incident response.

• Support and enhance our Python-based security analysis platform, including malware analysis engines, automated threat detection, and machine learning model workflows.

 Skills and Qualifications

• 5+ years of backend engineering experience, with recent experience in a JVM-based codebase.

• A track record of designing and owning distributed systems from start to finish.

• Experience with Rust, or a well-formed view of when it’s the right tool, and the ability to help guide a migration.

• Strong understanding of APIs, messaging systems (Kafka), and modern data stores (Postgres, DynamoDB, OpenSearch).

• Experience building services in a cloud-native environment, preferably AWS.

• Working knowledge of containers and Kubernetes.

• Comfortable working in a remote-first, asynchronous team environment.

 Bonus Skills and Qualifications

• Familiarity with functional programming patterns and idiomatic Scala.

• Experience with Databricks and ClickHouse (or similar lakehouse and analytical/OLAP data stores).

• Experience with Terraform, Helm, and GitHub Actions.

• Familiarity with observability tools (Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch).

• Prior work on security products, data pipelines, or high-availability systems.

• Python development experience, particularly with security analysis tools and malware detection frameworks (YARA, PE analysis, binary analysis).

• Familiarity with machine learning workflows, AutoML, and MLflow for model deployment and management.

• Experience with binary analysis libraries (LIEF, ssdeep, TLSH) and security tooling integration.

 Benefits:

 Halcyon offers the following benefits to eligible employees:

•
 Comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, and vision) with premiums paid in full for employees and dependents.

•
 401k plan with a generous employer contribution.

•
 Short and long-term disability coverage, basic life and AD&D insurance plans.

•
 Medical and dependent care FSA options.

•
 Flexible PTO policy.

•
 Parental leave.

•
 Generous equity offering.

 The Company reserves the right to modify or change these benefits programs at any time, with or without notice.​

 Base Salary Range : $120,000 - $170,000

 Bonus Target: 10%
 In accordance with applicable state and federal laws, the range provided is Halcyon’s reasonable estimate of the base compensation for this role. The actual amount may differ based on non-discriminatory factors such as experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, and location. Base pay is one part of the total package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work, and this role may be eligible for additional discretionary bonuses/incentives, and equity in the Company.

 We understand it takes a diverse team of highly intelligent, passionate, curious, and creative people to develop the exceptional product we are building. Our dynamic team has incredible perspectives to share, just as we know you do, and we take great pride in being an equal opportunity employer.

You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software.

You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share.

Headquarters: United States, Remote

 ROLE: Business Systems Administrator

 Location: United States, Remote

 This is a fully remote opportunity and can be worked from any location in the United States.

 ABOUT THE COMPANY:

 Salesloft is building the next era of enterprise revenue — one where teams make confident decisions powered by AI and real signals. By combining our scale, insights, and AI innovation, we're building the industry's first Predictive Revenue System, enabling humans and AI to work together to make smarter decisions and drive consistent growth.

 With thousands of customers using our platforms every day, we have an unmatched view into how revenue is actually won — the Revenue Context that reveals what happens, when, and with what outcome. This gives us a unique opportunity to transform an entire category and set a new benchmark for how modern revenue teams operate.

 Join us to help transform how companies around the world run revenue — and build the platform that will guide leading revenue teams into the future.

 THE OPPORTUNITY

 At Salesloft, our Business Systems Administrator, Customer Experience is critical to our company’s success. You will be a key member of our fast-growing and high-performing Business Systems team and will lead generating, scoping, solutioning, and executing process and efficiency improvement efforts across customer-focused systems. You will have a passionate, capable team supporting you.

 You will be responsible for the support, development, and maintenance of Salesforce and its related Customer Experience systems. You must own the pursuit of a world-class technology experience for our customers, while enabling scale and efficiency for internal customer experience teams - Support, Services, and Success. You need to have pride in the work you do and a passion for customer support and success.

 On a day to day basis, you will:

• Work with Services, Success, and Support teams to identify manual process that can be automated

• Scope, Plan, Recommend, and Deliver system solutions that help these teams meet their Objectives and Key Results

• Play a leading role in the exploration, design, build, delivery, and support of a redesigned and improved Customer Hub

 This role lives at the heart of how we Make Your Mark: you'll treat systems administration as a discipline — automating, documenting, and fixing root causes so the same issues don't recur. And in the spirit of how we are Customer Inspired — where every decision has a true north, and it's our customer — you'll administer access and configuration as the security controls they are, protecting the company and the data customers trust us with.

 WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 We are seeking a Salesforce CRM, and related customer experience systems, expert. Someone that can see the big picture, future state but has a keen eye for details. You will have a knack for spotting opportunities to improve systems and process, and are excited to work cross-functionally to make it happen. You are passionate to build relationships to help others succeed.

 If you’re looking for an opportunity to learn more, do more, and become more, then becoming a Business Systems Administrator is the career path for you!

 THE TEAM

 Our Salesloft’s Revenue Operations team is comprised of seasoned and up-and-coming operational experts.

 Values: Move as One, Evidence over Ego, Lead from the Front, Make Your Mark, Customer-Inspired.

 The Revenue Operations team consists of team members that work with Sales, Marketing, Customer Services, Finance, and IT to create systems to more efficiently prospect, forecast, close, onboard, and support customers. Team members conceptualize the strategic priorities for the company, develop execution plans, execute plans cross-functionally, and operationalize executed strategies for continuous improvement.

 THE SKILL SET

• Bachelor's degree

• 3+ years experience in a related role, Software (SaaS) experience is a plus

• 2-3 years experience administering Salesforce Service Cloud, Salesforce Knowledge, Live Agent, and Customer Communities preferred

• Salesforce Administrator certification is required

• Salesforce Service Cloud Consultant certification is a plus

• Demonstrated experience designing, revising and managing Salesforce Flows

• Ability to lead teams through change management and business transformations

• Excellent project management skills and the ability to collaborate with management and others in the company

• Disciplined, flexible, and autonomous work habits; we don't micromanage

• Understanding of the SaaS business model and culture is a plus

title: Senior AI Engineer - EU
description:
Headquarters: Germany (Remote) ; Ireland (Remote); Netherlands (Remote) ; Portugal (Remote) ; Spain (Remote) ; United Kingdom (Remote)

 Who we are

 Typeform is a refreshingly different form builder. We help over 150,000 businesses collect the data they need with forms, surveys, and quizzes that people enjoy. Designed to look striking and feel effortless to fill out, Typeform drives 500 million responses every year—and integrates with essential tools like Slack, Zapier, and Hubspot.

 Typeform is fully remote by design. For this role, we can hire candidates based in the UK, Ireland, Germany, Portugal, Spain or The Netherlands

 About the team

 The AI Engineering team builds the systems and capabilities behind Typeform’s AI products, including Research Flow, our platform for combining quantitative research with deeper qualitative insights.

 We use machine learning, large language models, RAG, and agentic systems to help customers collect, understand, and act on information in more conversational and personalised ways.

 Through Research Flow, this includes helping customers design studies, run AI-moderated conversations with adaptive follow-up questions, and turn responses into useful insights.

 The team owns the journey from experimentation through to production. This includes AI application development, evaluation, infrastructure, deployment, observability, reliability, and performance.

 You will work closely with Product Managers, Software Engineers, Data Scientists, Data Engineers, and Analytics teams to turn promising AI ideas into secure, scalable, and dependable customer experiences.

 About the role

 As a Senior AI Engineer at Typeform, you will be instrumental in building and evolving the AI capabilities behind Research Flow, alongside our broader AI products.

 Your work will help customers understand the “why” behind responses and move from research questions to informed decisions faster.

 Your scope will span generative AI applications, enterprise RAG systems, agentic workflows, model evaluation, machine learning pipelines, and the infrastructure required to run them reliably at scale.

 This is a hands-on engineering role with strong ownership. You will turn ideas and prototypes into production systems used by our customers, with direct influence on their quality and performance. You will also help define the technical standards for developing, evaluating, deploying, and monitoring AI across Typeform.

 Things you will do

 Build and deliver AI products

• Design, build, and deploy generative AI capabilities across Typeform’s products, with a key contribution to Research Flow.

• Develop applications using large language models, RAG, vector search, and agentic systems.

• Build services and APIs that allow product teams to integrate AI capabilities into customer experiences.

• Turn prototypes into reliable production systems with clear measures of performance and quality.

• Explore new ways for customers to collect, understand, and act on information using AI.

 Build scalable AI systems

• Design and operate machine learning services and workflows using Python, Docker, Kubernetes, and AWS.

• Build reliable pipelines for batch and real time processing using technologies such as Kafka and Airflow.

• Design solutions using vector databases to support retrieval, recommendations, personalisation, and semantic search.

• Use MLflow to manage experiments, model versions, registries, and deployments.

• Improve the reliability, performance, scalability, and cost efficiency of our AI systems.

 Evaluate and improve AI quality

• Build automated evaluation pipelines for generative AI applications, including the conversational and analytical capabilities behind Research Flow.

• Develop benchmarks that measure accuracy, relevance, reliability, fairness, latency, and cost.

• Evaluate retrieval strategies, including chunking, embeddings, context selection, and reranking.

• Monitor AI systems in production and identify opportunities to improve their quality and performance.

• Create safeguards that reduce unexpected behaviour and protect customer data.

 Shape our AI engineering practice

• Establish reusable patterns and technical standards for building, evaluating, and releasing AI systems.

• Help teams make informed decisions about models, frameworks, infrastructure, performance, and cost.

• Apply strong engineering practices across testing, security, observability, version control, and deployment.

• Share technical knowledge and support the development of other engineers.

• Keep up with relevant AI research, tools, and engineering practices, applying what is useful to Typeform.

 Collaborate across Typeform

• Partner with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Data Engineering, and Analytics teams to connect AI investments with customer and business needs.

• Work with Data Scientists to turn experiments and models into reliable production services.

• Communicate technical concepts, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to technical and nontechnical partners.

• Contribute to technical planning and help shape the direction of AI across Typeform.

 What you bring

• At least four years of experience building and deploying machine learning or AI systems in production.

• Strong Python and software engineering skills.

• Experience building production services using Python frameworks such as FastAPI.

• Practical experience developing generative AI applications using large language models, RAG, tool use, or agentic systems.

• Experience with frameworks such as PyTorch, LangChain, LangGraph, or similar technologies.

• A strong understanding of enterprise RAG systems, including chunking, embeddings, retrieval, reranking, evaluation, and monitoring.

• Experience creating automated evaluations for generative AI applications.

• Experience with AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and continuous integration and deployment practices.

• Experience using services such as AWS SageMaker or AWS Bedrock.

• Experience with Kafka, vector databases, or other technologies used for real time and high dimensional data processing.

• Experience managing machine learning workflows using MLflow.

• Experience monitoring production systems with tools such as Datadog or OpenSearch.

• The ability to balance quality, speed, reliability, scalability, and cost when making technical decisions.

• Strong communication skills and experience collaborating with Product, Engineering, and Data teams.

 Extra awesome

• Experience working in a B2B SaaS product company.

• Experience with orchestration tools such as Airflow or Argo Workflows.

• Familiarity with SQL, Spark, Snowflake, or other data processing technologies.

• Experience building systems that combine structured data, unstructured data, and generative AI.

• Experience with AI security, privacy, responsible AI, prompt injection protection, or data leakage prevention.

• Experience improving the latency and cost of AI systems operating at scale.

 *Typeform drives hundreds of millions of interactions each year, enabling conversational, human-centered experiences across the globe. We move as one team , empowering our collective efforts by valuing each individual’s unique perspective. This fosters strong bonds grounded in respect, transparency, and trust. We champion our diverse customer base by anticipating their needs and addressing their challenges with priority. Committed to excellence, we hold high expectations for ourselves and each other, continuously striving to deliver exceptional results.

 We are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and stand firmly against discrimination and harassment of any kind—whether based on race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. Everyone is welcome here.
